    Session · 9:15 AM ET · weekdays

    The Pre-Open Check

    Fifteen minutes before the bell the whole committee revalidates the briefing against futures, pre-market prints, the OI-conversion audit, analyst moves and the 8:30 prints, and the Executive signs a verdict.

    What the check is#

    At 9:15 AM ET, fifteen minutes before the open, the board reconvenes over the morning's run and asks one question of the overnight tape: does it confirm the briefing, or does yesterday's flow look like a pump fake? The session productizes a revalidation the desk did by hand on 2026-07-24, when a "-4.8%" Brent print turned out to be a contract roll and an option-volume spike turned out to have gone home flat. It runs as boardroom.preopen.run_preopen_review() on the weekday scheduler — the time is editable under Settings — or on demand with Run pre-open check on the morning dashboard. A run that has already been checked is skipped; the button forces a fresh check, which replaces the stored one for that run.

    The overnight packet#

    Every collector degrades independently: a failed fetch is a missing row, never an aborted check.

    Futures tape
    ES, NQ, RTY, CL, BZ, GC and ZB from two days of 15-minute pre/post bars — yesterday's final print against the latest, as an overnight %. A CL-vs-BZ divergence of more than four points flags the Brent print as a probable front-month roll, per the 2026-07-24 lesson, and tells the room to trust WTI for the crude read.
    Pre-market prints
    Each lead's latest 5-minute pre/post print against its briefing price, as vs_briefing_pct; every seat also sees the move signed in the lead's favor.
    OI-conversion audit
    For every option lead, the stored contract is found in today's chain and held_ratio = oi_now / yesterday_volume is computed: did yesterday's volume convert into held open interest overnight, or was it day-traded? Below 0.35 reads as exit, below 0.60 as trim.
    Analyst moves
    Upgrades and downgrades over the last two days across the universe plus the lead tickers, with a sector rollup and the lead-specific rows pulled out.
    Economic prints
    The 8:30–9:00 tape from the BLS, BEA and Census feeds plus keyword-matched domestic headlines — CPI, payrolls, GDP, PCE, ISM and the rest — as prints and one-line summaries.
    Flagged headlines
    Fresh US and world headlines matching the flag list — truce, ceasefire, tariff, sanction, Fed and FOMC, rate cut or hike, OPEC, escalation, shutdown, stimulus, default, embargo — up to twelve, deduplicated by title.
    Gap context (the Glazier)
    Per lead: the gap from the prior close in % and in 14-day ATR multiples; where the print sits in the prior day's range (above the high, upper range, lower range, below the low); a taxonomy hint — common, breakaway candidate (an ATR or more out of a compressed five-day range), runaway candidate (continuing a three-day run of closes) — and a doctrine base-rate note from Bulkowski's fill statistics and Andrews' zone odds.

    The panel: fourteen reads and a verdict#

    Since round 11 the whole grading committee sits — all thirteen graders plus the Skeptic, in speaking order — and each files one market read and one action per lead:

    Market readMeaningPer-lead actionMeaning
    CONFIRMED MOVEthe overnight tape confirms the briefingHOLDcarry the morning thesis to the bell
    PUMP FAKEyesterday's flow or move is not holdingEXIT · TRIMout before the open, or cut the size
    UNDECIDEDneither confirmation nor collapseUPGRADE · WATCHthe case got stronger overnight; or nothing has broken yet

    Each seat gets the common context — the futures tape, the lead rows with their pre-market prints, the flagged headlines — and its own data slice: Flow and the Croupier get the OI audit; the Chartist gets the support, resistance, SMA and Fibonacci levels stored with the briefing; the Glazier gets the gap contexts; Sam, the Croupier, the Skeptic, the Watchdog and the Domestic Desk get the econ prints and the analyst tape; the Timekeeper gets the cycle picture. Every prompt also carries the seat's five latest journal lessons and its Pyramid rank line. In AI mode that is one JSON-schema call per seat, fourteen in all, and one more for the chair. The Executive then signs the final verdict, a three-to-six-sentence memo update that says what changed and what stands, and one lead_updates row per lead — an action and a note — which are the rows the dashboard turns into corner chips.

    Without an API key#

    Mock mode is deterministic and data-true, and its rules are the clearest statement of what each seat watches before the bell:

    • Flow — held ratio below 0.35 is exit, below 0.60 is trim; the market read averages the audited contracts: "yesterday's volume was day-traded, not held. That flow was a pump fake."
    • Dagger — the pre-market move signed by direction: ≤ −2.0% exit, ≤ −0.75% trim, ≥ +1.5% upgrade; confirmed when two or more leads print with the briefing and more print with it than against, inside a 0.3% dead zone.
    • The Chartist — a print through the stored support (for a long) or resistance (for a short) is a level that failed overnight: trim, or exit if it broke by more than 1%; a print through the far level is an upgrade.
    • The Glazier — rides a breakaway candidate, exits a position that fades one, trims a common gap of an ATR or more behind the entry, and declines to grade a window it cannot measure.
    • Sam — an analyst downgrade on the name is trim, an upgrade is upgrade, a signed print of −2% or worse is exit: never counter-trend.
    • The Oracle flags only moves of 3% or more, as "Mr. Market's morning mood"; Graham warns against chasing a gap-up of 2% or more; the Black Swan presses the sheet's biggest gap when it is an option already paying; the Watchdog watches 2.5% moves with no public catalyst; the two desks attribute moves to the flagged headlines and the overnight world tape; the Timekeeper reads the morning against a projected cycle phase; the Skeptic exits on a downgrade or a dead held ratio.
    • The Executive — the verdict is the panel's vote; per lead the most cautious action any seat cast wins — exit over trim over watch over upgrade over hold — and the note names who drove it.

    Where it shows#

    On the morning dashboard the Pre-open check — 9:15 panel appears when the latest check belongs to the displayed run: the verdict chip (PUMP FAKE red, CONFIRMED MOVE green, UNDECIDED amber), the Executive's memo update, an Econ strip of up to five summary lines, an Analyst strip with the top upgrades and downgrades as chips and a sector rollup line, one verdict chip per panelist with its comment in the tooltip, and a Details expander holding the futures chips (and the roll warning when it fires) and the OI-conversion table — ticker, contract, volume → OI, held ratio colored by threshold, last. Before any check exists the panel reads "Pre-open check runs at 9:15 ET" beside the run button. Every lead card whose ticker has an Executive action wears the corner chip, tooltip carrying the note. The Archive replays the check for any past day.

    Guards and storage#

    One review per run, replaced on a forced re-run, in preopen_reviews (the compact packet and the verdicts: each panelist's market read plus the Executive's verdict, memo update and lead updates). On a weekend or holiday with no run today, the check reviews the most recent completed run. The scheduled time is preopen_hour / preopen_minute (defaults 9:15 ET); a lock refuses a second concurrent check. Nothing here executes anything — the actions are research notes on a research briefing.

    API#

    GET /api/preopen/latest
    {"review": {run_id, review_date, packet, verdicts, created_at} | null, "members": [...]}
    POST /api/preopen/trigger
    Starts a forced check in a background thread → {"started": bool, "progress": {...}}
    GET /api/preopen/progress
    Stage chip: collect, guard, panel (hearing each seat), executive, persist.
    Settings
    preopen_hour / preopen_minute via GET/POST /api/settings; saving reschedules the job.
